cohort: 314 pregnant women attending antenatal clinics in Abeokuta North Local Government Area, Nigeria
finding: The prevalence of antenatal depression was 24.5%, and several factors were significantly associated with it, including attending a public health facility, younger maternal age, single marital status, lower education level, larger family size, unplanned pregnancy, coexisting medical conditions, history of C-section, alcohol use during pregnancy, and gender-based abuse.
